10.1002_adma.75458: The pervasive accumulation and recalcitrance of micro/nanoplastics in ecosystems pose severe environmental and health challenges, demanding innovative solutions that integrate remediation with resource recovery. In this study, we report magnetically driven Au nanoparticles/helical‐Mn/N‐doped carbon nanotubes (AMNC) micromotors engineered for the integrated capture, time‐resolved monitoring, and catalytic upcycling of polystyrene (PS) micro/nanoplastics. The AMNC micromotors achieve near‐complete degradation of PS, producing valuable benzoic acid with a yield of approximately 60%. The dynamic motion of micromotors under a magnetic field enables active enrichment of micro/nanoplastics, while the electromagnetic “hot spots” at the Au‐micromotor interface enable sensitive, in situ surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) tracking with a detection limit of 0.17 µg/mL. Mechanistic studies reveal that N‐doping and manganese carbide species synergistically enhance peroxymonosulfate activation and electron transfer, with density functional theory calculations identifying the SO 4 •‒ ‐mediated attack on the PS backbone as the rate‐determining step. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse water matrices and under scale‐up conditions, with a machine learning model ( R 2 = 1.0) accurately predicting degradation efficiency. Techno‐economic analysis confirms the economic viability of the process and a significantly reduced environmental footprint. This intelligent platform integrates pollution control with value‐added conversion for sustainable plastic waste management.
10.1002_smll.74629: This work demonstrates the synthesis of S‐doped MoSe 2 (S‐MoSe 2 ) quantum dots (QDs) grown on MXene‐derived 2D rutile TiO 2 nanosheets (MTS) for highly efficient and durable noble metal‐free catalyst for both photocatalytic and electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) under universal pH conditions. The incorporation of sulfur atoms effectively modulates the electronic structure of MoSe 2 , enhancing active site density and improving charge transfer efficiency, while 2D MTS provides a high surface area support and strong interfacial interaction. The synthesized S‐MoSe 2 /MTS catalyst demonstrates the superior visible‐light absorption, leading to highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen production yield of 1054 µmol·h −1 ·g −1 with excellent durability. Furthermore, the S‐MoSe 2 /MTS catalyst performs the outstanding electrochemical activity of HER with low overpotentials and long‐term stability under pH‐universal conditions. The density functional theory (DFT) study shows that the sulfur doping in MoSe 2 decreases the energy barrier for water dissociation and tunes the Gibbs free energy of hydrogen intermediates to values favorable for catalytic reactions. In addition, the built‐in electric field between S‐MoSe 2 and MTS promotes charge separation and improves electrical conductivity. This synergistic effect leads to excellent photocatalytic and electrocatalytic hydrogen generation. This study provides a promising strategy for noble metal‐free catalysts with excellent photocatalytic and electrocatalytic performance for hydrogen production.
10.1016_j.cej.2025.171236: The aqueous zinc (Zn)-based energy storage system (AZESS) offers low cost and high safety, making it a promising candidate for energy storage devices. However, its practical application is hindered by dendritic growth and side reactions at the anode side. To overcome these challenges, a multi-level modulation strategy is proposed based on a multi-component hydrogel electrolyte to precisely regulate the Zn 2+ solvation structure, hydrogen-bond (H-bond) network, and deposition behavior. This tailored electrolyte suppresses interfacial water aggregation, mitigates water-induced side reactions, and enables uniform Zn deposition/dissolution, thereby effectively inhibiting dendrite growth and enhancing interfacial stability. As a result, the Zn//Zn symmetric cell using this hydrogel demonstrates remarkable durability, along with a high coulombic efficiency. Moreover, the assembled Zn//Activated carbon (AC) capacitor exhibits outstanding long-term performance, maintaining an impressive capacity retention of 99.55 % and high coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8 % after 35,000 cycles. This strategy provides a promising pathway for the rational design of advanced electrolytes toward high-performance Zinc-ion capacitors (ZICs). A hydrogel electrolyte is designed to enhance the stability of Zn-metal anode by optimizing Zn 2+ solvation, reconstructing the hydrogen-bonding network and tuning Zn deposition behavior. This multi-level regulation strategy effectively suppresses dendrite growth and H 2 O-induced side reactions, enabling good reversibility and long-term cycling stability in Zn//Zn cells and Zn//AC capacitors, offering new insights for advanced electrolyte design for aqueous Zn-based energy storage systems. • A multi-level modulation strategy enables regulation of Zn 2+ solvation structure and hydrogen-bond networks through a hydrogel electrolyte. • Interfacial water activity, dendrites and side reactions are greatly suppressed. • Regulated Zn nucleation enables uniform plating/stripping and long-term interfacial stability. • The Zn//AC capacitor achieves 99.55 % capacity retention and 99.8 % CE after 35,000 cycles.
10.1016_j.wroa.2026.100502: • EPFRs generate on PS MPs surface in darkness • PS MPs reduce Ag + to Ag 0 NPs via EPFRs. • EPFRs generate O 2 •− that can further reduce Ag + . • EPFRs also yield 1 O 2 and •OH, oxidizing Ag 0 NPs to Ag 2 O. • PS MPs-mediated Ag + transformation suppresses toxicity of Ag + The co-occurrence of nanoplastics (NPs) and Ag + has drawn public attention, and NPs-driven transformation of Ag⁺ has been widely documented under sunlight. However, the role of NPs in Ag + transformation remains poorly understood under dark conditions. We found that environmentally persistent free radicals (EPFRs) generated on polystyrene (PS) NPs surfaces in dark are fundamentally distinct from those formed under sunlight. The Ag + markedly amplified EPFR formation and accelerated oxidative aging of PS NPs, as reflected by a higher carbonyl index compared with PS NPs alone (CI; 0.313 vs 0.107). Moreover, these EPFRs drive Ag + transformation in the dark. Specifically, the EPFRs reduce Ag + to Ag 0 nanoparticles ( k reduction = 2.7 × 10 ‒3 d ‒1 ), either via direct electron transfer or indirectly by generating O 2 •− as the primary reductant that subsequently drives Ag + reduction. These EPFRs can further oxidize newly formed Ag 0 to Ag 2 O nanoparticles by generating 1 O 2 , and •OH, yielding Ag 0 /Ag 2 O hetero-nanoparticles. Correspondingly, this NPs-mediated change in Ag speciation significantly suppressed Ag accumulation and alleviated oxidative stress in zebrafish larvae in natural waters, thereby significantly increasing 8-h survival (56.7% vs 40.0% for Ag + alone; p < 0.05). Therefore, the presence of PS NPs should be explicitly considered when assessing Ag + risks in natural aquatic ecosystems, including under dark conditions.
10.1021_acsenergylett.6c01690: Formamidinium lead iodide (FAPbI3) perovskites are promising for high-performance solar cells; however, the low surface energy of self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) impedes α-phase nucleation in inverted devices. Here, we report a formamidinium (FA)-solvent intermediate-mediated self-seeding crystallization strategy to enable quality α-phase FAPbI3. By employing N-formylmorpholine (NFM) as a non-toxic solvent, (FA···NFM)PbI3 intermediates are formed, thereby lowering the phase-transition barrier and promoting the spontaneous formation of α-phase nuclei at the early stage of crystallization. These preformed nuclei serve as intrinsic seeds, facilitating rapid nucleation and orientated crystal growth. Consequently, NFM-based devices achieve efficiencies of 26.41% and 26.56% using 2-methoxyethanol (2-Me) and N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) as primary solvents, respectively, with a 1 cm2 device reaching 25.47%. The unencapsulated devices retain 85% and 90% of their initial efficiencies after 1200 h illumination and 1400 h thermal aging at 85 °C, respectively.
